title: Default Parameter Values
hints: Parameters with default values can be left out at the call site.
Write `greet(_:greeting:punctuation:)` with defaults, then call it three different ways depending on the index.
jsBridge: Like JS default parameters (`function greet(name, greeting = 'Hello')`), except Swift defaults can sit on any parameter because labels disambiguate. You can skip the middle one, which JS can't do without passing `undefined`.

compass.q: JS: to use the default for `greeting` but set `punctuation`, you pass `undefined`. Why doesn't Swift need that?
Default parameters vs overloads: which keeps a public API evolvable without breaking callers?
Are default values evaluated at each call, like JS, or once? Can a default reference another parameter?
SwiftUI modifiers are full of defaults, like `padding(_ edges: = .all, _ length: = nil)`. Find one and read its signature.
